questions.text: P and Q can do a piece of work in 24 and 20 days respectively. They started the work together but P left after some days and the remaining work is completed by Q in 9 days. After how many days P left the work.
questions.explanation:
Suppose total work = 120 units (LCM of 24 and 20)

⇒ Efficiency of P = 120/24 = 5

⇒ Efficiency of Q = 120/20 = 6

They started the work together, but P left after some days and the remaining work is completed by Q in 9 days

Suppose P left after ‘x’ days

⇒ (5 + 6) × x + 6 × 9 = 120

⇒ 11x = 66

⇒ x = 6

∴ P left after 6 days.

questions.text: 16 women take 12 days to complete a piece of work which can be completed by 12 men in 8 days. 16 men start working and after 3 days, 10 men left while 4 women joined them. In how many days, the remaining work will get completed?
questions.explanation:
Let W and M be the efficiencies of a woman and a man respectively,

⇒ 16W × 12 = 12M × 8

⇒ W : M = 1 : 2

Suppose W = 1 and M = 2

Since 16 women take 12 days to complete a piece of work

⇒ Total work = 16 × 12 = 192 units

⇒ Work done by 16 men in 3 days = 16 × 2 × 3 = 96 units

⇒ Remaining work = 192 - 96 = 96 units

Suppose it will be competed in ‘x’ days

⇒ 96 = 6 × 2 × x + 4 × 1 × x

⇒ 16x = 96

⇒ x = 6

∴ Remaining work will get complete in 6 days.

questions.text: A is 20% less efficient than B. A, when working alone, takes 60 days to finish the job. A works alone for ‘x’ days. After that, B joins him and the two work together to finish the job in exactly 40 days (counting from the day A began working alone). What is the value of ‘x’?
questions.explanation:
Given A is 20% less efficient than B

If B can complete 5 units of work in a day then A can complete [5 - (20% of 5)] = 4 units of work of same work in a day

Given A takes 60 days to finish the work

Total work of A = 60 × 4 = 240 units

A works alone for ‘x’ days and the two work together for (40 - x) days

Using the concept of man days, we get

4x + [(40 - x) × 9] = 240

⇒ 4x + 360 - 9x = 240

⇒ 9x - 4x = 360 - 240

⇒ 5x = 120

⇒ x = 120/5

⇒ x = 24 days

∴ Required number of days = 24

questions.text: A can do a piece of work in 20 days and B can do the same piece of work in 30 days. A and B started the work together in the first 10 days A worked with half of his efficiency and so does B. Now in how many days does the remaining work get completed when both of them work with their full efficiency?
questions.explanation:
Suppose the total work = 60 Units

Efficiency of A = 60/20 = 3 units/days

Efficiency of B = 60/30 = 2 units/days

Given that A and B started work together but with half of their efficiency

1.5 + 1 = 2.5 units /days total efficiency of A and B

Work completed = 10 × 2.5 = 25 units

Work left = (60 - 25) = 35 units

Now they work with their full efficiency

Total efficiency = (3 + 2) = 5 units/days

∴ No. of days taken by A and B together = 35/5 = 7 days

questions.text: A bucket can be filled by a pipe in 10 minutes and by another pipe in 40 minutes. Both the pipes are kept open for 5 minutes and then the first pipe is closed. After this, how much more time will be required to fill the complete bucket?
questions.explanation:
Part filled by pipe A in 1 minute = 1/10

Part filled by pipe B in 1 minute = 1/40

(A + B)’s 10 minute work = 5 × (1/10 + 1/40) = 5/8

Remaining work = 1 – 5/8 = 3/8

⇒ 1/40 : 3/8 = 1 : x

⇒ 1/15 = 1/x

⇒ x = 15

∴ remaining time is 15 minutes

questions.text: A can do a work in 1/3rd time as taken by B, while B takes twice the time taken by C. They together completes a work in 12 days, such that A and B left the work 6 and 4 days respectively before its completion, while C completed the work alone. In how many days will A do the work alone?
questions.explanation:
Let A takes ‘x’ days to do the work alone

A’s 1 day work = 1/x

∵ A takes 1/3rd time as taken by B, time taken by B = 3x days

B’s 1 day work = 1/3x

∵ B takes twice time as taken by C, time taken by C = 3x/2 days

C’s 1 day work = 2/3x

To complete the job, A worked for 12 – 6 = 6 days, B worked for 12 – 4 – 8 days and C worked for 12 days

⇒ Total work done = 6(1/x) + 8(1/3x) + 12(2/3x) = 1

⇒ 50/3x = 1

⇒ x = 50/3 days

∴ A will complete the work alone in 50/3 days

questions.text: 4 boys and 6 girls complete a task in 24 days. If the girls are at least half as efficient as the boys, but not more efficient than the boys, what is the range of the number of days for 6 girls and 2 boys to complete the same task?
questions.explanation:
4b and 6g finish in 24 days

In one day, 4b + 6g = 1/24 of task

Now, just substitute extreme values to get the whole range

If a girl is half as efficient as boy

4b + 3b = 1/24, 7b = 1/24, b = 1/168

6g + 2b = 3b + 2b = 5b, 5b will take 168/5 days = 33.6 days

If a girl is as efficient as a boy

4b + 6g finish in 24 days

10b finish 1/24 of task in a day

6g + 2b = 8b, 8b will take 240/8 = 30 days to finish the task

∴ The range = 30 to 33.6 days

questions.text: Aman and Nisha can do a work in 16 days and 24 days respectively. Beginning with Aman if the work is to be done on alternate basis by both of them than in how many days the work will get completed?
questions.explanation:
Let the total work = 48 units

Efficiency of Aman = 48/16 = 3 units/day

Efficiency of Nisha = 48/24 = 2 units/day

Since they are working alternatively then we will calculate the two days work of both of them

⇒ 3 + 2 = 5 units of work in two days

Since they do 5 units of work in 2 days

Hence, they will do 45 units of work in 18 days

And the rest of the work is now be completed by Aman in = 3/3 = 1 day

∴ Total days will be 19 for completing the whole work

questions.text: A and B can finish a job in 10 days while B and C can do it in 18 days. A started the job, worked for 5 days then B worked for 10 days and the remaining job was finished by C in 15 days. In how many days could C alone have finished the whole job?
questions.explanation:
Let A, B and C alone can finish the job in x, y and z days

Let the total work be 1

⇒ One-day work of A, B and C be 1/x, 1/y and 1/z

⇒ 10/x + 10/y = 1

⇒ 18/y + 18/z = 1

⇒ 5/x + 10/y + 15/z = 1 

Taking 1/x = u, 1/y = v and 1/z =w

⇒ 10u + 10v = 1 ……eq1

⇒ 18v + 18w = 1  ……eq2

⇒ 5u + 10v + 15w = 1   ……eq3

Solving equation 1, 2 and 3 we get

⇒ w = 1/45

∴ C alone can finish the work in = 1/u = 45 days

questions.text: A alone can paint a building in 15 days and B can do the same work in 20 days. Both were jointly hired to do the work for Rs. 6000. After 3 days B left and C joined who performed 1/3 of the remaining work. Calculate the wages of A, B, and C separately.
questions.explanation:
Given:

A alone can paint a building in 15 days.

B can do the same work in 20 days.

Both were jointly hired to do the work for Rs. 6000.

Concept:

"Wages is proportional to work done"

Calculation:

⇒ A’s income per day = 6000/15 = 400

⇒ B’s income per day = 6000/20 = 300

⇒ A’s income in 3 days = 400 × 3 = 1200

⇒ B’s income in 3 days = 300 × 3 = 900

Now, B doesn’t work further but A still have done 2/3 of the remaining work.

⇒ Amount left for remaining work = 6000 – 1200 – 900 = 3900

⇒ Amount A will get = (2/3) × 3900 = 2 × 1300 = 2600

⇒ Amount C will get = (1/3) × 3900 = 1 × 1300 = 1300

⇒ A’s total income = 1200 + 2600 = 3800

∴ The income of A, B and C are Rs. 3800, Rs. 900 and Rs. 1300 respectively
